values.condition: He-sdO US 708, described as a hypervelocity star and the fastest unbound star known

evidence.quote: the hypervelocity star US 708, a He-sdO moving with\mathrm { { \bar { \sim } 1 2 0 0 k m s ^ { - 1 } } }.

notes: US 708: The paper directly names US 708 as the hypervelocity object and calls it the fastest unbound star known in our Galaxy (T:p2-b4), while the abstract reports its discovery (T:p1-b6); it is therefore retained as candidates_found. CD−30°11223 (T:p2-b4) is a close sdB+WD binary discussed as a possible double-detonation progenitor, not as a present-day Galactic unbound star, and is not counted.

US 708: T:p2-b4 reports that US 708, a He-sdO, is moving with about 1200 km/s and is the fastest unbound star known. The paper does not explicitly label this as a line-of-sight or Galactic rest-frame speed; it is recorded as a Galactic rest-frame speed because of the hypervelocity-star context. No other US 708 quantities are reported.
